subject: Agriculture
title: The Meat Paradox
description: A fast breakdown of The Meat Paradox for builders.

hook.text: Most people love animals and eat them too. Psychologists call this cognitive conflict the meat paradox.

buildup.text: Studies show people who eat meat rate farm animals as less intelligent and less capable of suffering.

discovery.text: This is motivated reasoning—adjusting beliefs to reduce guilt about a behavior you enjoy.

twist.text: When people visit farms and interact with animals, their willingness to eat those species drops significantly.

climax.text: The meat industry deliberately distances consumers from production. Packaging shows green fields, not feedlots.

punchline.text: We eat what we don't see. Visibility changes behavior.

quiz.question: What is the 'meat paradox'?
options: People love animals yet eat them, using motivated reasoning to reduce guilt
